title: Smoky Chicken Tinga
summary: Chicken thighs simmered in a smoky chipotle and tomato sauce, then shredded into it. Perfect piled on tostadas or tucked into tacos.

creator.bio: Sample creator. Everyday Mexican family cooking: tacos, rice and slow-simmered sauces.

steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden, about 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
success_cues: Onions are soft and golden at the edges
warnings: Hot oil can spit; add food away from your body and keep the handle turned inward.

steps.instruction: Add the crushed tomatoes, chipotles with their sauce, oregano, salt and half a cup of water. Simmer 5 minutes.
success_cues: Sauce is brick red and gently bubbling
warnings: Chipotle sauce stains and burns eyes; wash hands after chopping.

steps.instruction: Nestle the chicken thighs into the sauce, cover and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, turning once.
success_cues: Meat pulls apart easily with a fork
A thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F (74°C)
warnings: Raw chicken: wash hands, board and knife after handling, and keep it away from ready-to-eat food. Check the thickest piece reaches 165°F (74°C) with a thermometer; color alone is not a reliable sign.
steps.creator_note: Thighs stay juicy here. Breast dries out if you go this long.

steps.instruction: Lift the chicken out onto a board, shred it with two forks and return it to the sauce. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes so the sauce clings.
success_cues: Sauce coats the shreds and no thin liquid pools in the pan
warnings: Use a clean board, not the one that held raw chicken.

steps.instruction: Taste for salt and finish with cilantro if using.
success_cues: Smoky, slightly spicy and well seasoned

creator_notes: Even better the next day. It freezes well too.
dietary_warnings: Check the chipotle can label; some brands contain wheat or soy.
